mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 270 CDI or 300 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a C270 CDI or C300 CDI typically costs between £600 and £5,000 depending on the engine code and condition. Used OM612 units start from £600-£1,400, reconditioned from £1,800-£3,000, and fully rebuilt OM642 engines from £2,800-£5,000. Labour for supply & fit adds £500-£1,000.

mainEntity.name: What is 'Black Death' and does it affect the C-Class 270 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: 'Black Death' refers to injector seal failure that affects OM612 engines. The copper washer seal between the injector and cylinder head degrades, allowing combustion gases to escape. This creates hard, black carbon deposits around the injector. Symptoms include a ticking or chuffing noise, a strong diesel smell in the cabin, hissing sounds from the engine, and visible black tar-like residue. If left untreated, the injector can seize in the cylinder head, requiring expensive extraction and head repairs.

mainEntity.name: Does the C-Class 270 CDI or 300 CDI have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the OM612 (C270 CDI) and OM642 (C300 CDI) use timing chains, not belts. The OM612 features a front-mounted duplex roller chain, which is generally robust with a service life of 200,000-250,000 kilometres. The OM642 features a duplex roller chain per cylinder bank. Neither has a scheduled replacement interval, but tensioner wear can occur at higher mileages.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz C-Class 270 CDI or 300 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W203 C270 CDI is typically worth £1,500-£4,000 - a full engine replacement often exceeds the car's value, making a used engine or targeted repair more economical. A W204 C300 CDI is worth £5,000-£12,000 - a rebuilt OM642 engine (£2,800-£5,000) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. Always compare the cost of repair against the car's market value.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the C270 CDI and C300 CDI engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: The C270 CDI uses the OM612 2.7-litre five-cylinder diesel (170 hp, 400 Nm), fitted to the W203 generation from 2000-2005. The C300 CDI uses the OM642 3.0-litre V6 diesel (231 hp, 540 Nm), fitted to the W204 generation from 2011-2014. The OM642 offers significantly more power and refinement but has a well-documented oil cooler seal leak. The OM612 is a simpler design with fewer complex emissions systems.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz C-Class 300 CDI to lose oil?

acceptedAnswer.text: The C300 CDI's OM642 V6 engine is known for oil cooler seal failure, which causes oil to leak from the Vee of the engine. Symptoms include a 'Check Oil Level' message, decreasing oil level measurements, and oil stains or puddles underneath the vehicle. The leak is very difficult to inspect from the top of the engine, and most owners discover it when oil starts dripping from the back of the engine. Mercedes Service Bulletin LI18.30-P-055434 addresses this issue.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 270 CDI / 300 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The C270 CDI and C300 CDI badges represent the flagship diesel offerings across two generations of the Mercedes-Benz C-Class. The C270 CDI arrived with the W203 generation in 2000, powered by Mercedes' robust five-cylinder OM612 diesel. The C300 CDI joined the range with the facelifted W204 in 2011, featuring the smooth and torquey OM642 V6 diesel - a significant step up in refinement and performance.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes-Benz C-Class 270 CDI / 300 CDI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The C270 CDI and C300 CDI have been powered by two distinct diesel engine families - the five-cylinder OM612 (W203) and the V6 OM642 (W204). The OM612 is renowned for durability with a front-mounted duplex timing chain but suffers from injector seal failure and fuel pump issues. The OM642 offers smooth V6 power but has a well-documented oil cooler seal weakness. Rebuilt C270 CDI and C300 CDI engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components designed to address the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM612 Injector Seal Failure - "Black Death" Carbon Buildup in the C270 CDI
problems.rootCause: The copper washer seal between the injector and cylinder head degrades over time, allowing combustion gases to escape past the seal. The escaping gas mixes with carbon and unburnt fuel, creating hard, black, crusty deposits around the injector. The OM612 engine is known for injector issues, which can cause rough idling, increased fuel consumption, and poor acceleration. A strong diesel smell in the cabin often gives the problem away before the "Black Death" gets too bad.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove one injector, clean seat, replace copper washer and clamp bolt
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; prevents injector seizure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: All five injector seals replaced, carbon removal from bores, leak-off testing
repairOptions.longevity: For moderate carbon buildup; specialist approach significantly cheaper

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Seized injector drilling/extraction, cylinder head removal, injector bore machining
repairOptions.longevity: Required if injector cannot be extracted non-destructively

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W203 C270 CDI is worth £1,500-£4,000. A full engine replacement often exceeds the car's value - a used engine or targeted injector seal repair is usually more economical. For W204 C300 CDI models worth £5,000-£12,000, a rebuilt OM642 with warranty can be a worthwhile investment.
problems.recommendation: The "Black Death" is insidious but slow-moving. If you hear a ticking or chuffing noise that changes with engine speed, or smell diesel fumes in the cabin, inspect the injector area immediately. Caught early, an £180-£300 single seal replacement is cheap peace of mind. Replacing all five copper washers at once is often recommended due to similar wear patterns.

problems.group: OM612 High-Pressure Fuel Pump & Timing Chain Issues
problems.h4: OM612 High-Pressure Fuel Pump & Timing Chain Issues - Fuel Delivery and Chain Wear
problems.rootCause: The high-pressure fuel pump can fail, with particles damaging injectors. The timing chain tensioner and guide wear can also occur, though less frequently than on petrol variants. The timing chain service life rarely exceeds 200,000-250,000 kilometres before tensioner and stretch issues arise.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace HPFP, flush fuel system, inspect injectors
repairOptions.longevity: Required if pump has failed; check for debris contamination
Viable if caught early; front-mounted chain makes access easier

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new fuel pump and timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Best long-term value on higher-mileage cars

problems.recommendation: If your C270 CDI experiences rough running or hard starting, have the high-pressure fuel pump and injectors inspected. Fuel contamination can damage precision injector tips and high-pressure pump components. A £500-£900 pump replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Regular fuel filter changes and using quality diesel are essential preventative measures.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM612 fuel pump and timing chain repair for your C270 CDI

problems.h4: OM642 Oil Cooler Seal Leak - The V6 Diesel's Most Common Weakness
problems.rootCause: The oil cooler seals in the OM642 V6 degrade over time, causing oil to leak from the Vee of the engine. Mercedes Service Bulletin LI18.30-P-055434 addresses this issue. Symptoms include a "Check Oil Level" message, decreasing oil level measurements, and oil stains or puddles underneath the vehicle. The leak is very difficult to inspect from the top of the engine, and most owners discover it when oil starts dripping from the back of the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of oil cooler seals, intake manifold removal, oil flush, replacement of oil-soaked wiring loom sections
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; prevents oil starvation damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Oil cooler seals plus turbocharger inspection, oil feed line cleaning, full oil system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil level has dropped significantly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new oil cooler seals, upgraded loom, and rebuilt turbocharger
repairOptions.longevity: Required if oil starvation has caused bearing or turbo damage

problems.recommendation: The OM642 oil cooler leak is a well-documented and predictable failure. Check your W204 C300 CDI's driveway for oil spots and inspect the loom near the ECU for oil wicking. Catch it early, and an £800-£1,200 specialist seal replacement is straightforward. On a C Class worth £5,000-£12,000, if the engine has already suffered oil starvation damage, replacement is the only safe route. A pal had the OM642 oil cooler seal leak issue in a 2007 CLK at only 70k miles and got rid of it because of repair costs quoted at £1,200+.
